week, let me clarify them.
In short, yes, both the pre-filled Object of interest (for the Object
Detection project) and the pre-labelled instrument bounding box
representing the ROI (for the Instrument Readout project) will come from
our product users or be created using their input.

For now, I suggest the following to unblock the training:

extinguisher' or 'emergency exit sign' as the object of interest. If it's
not too confusing, let's train the annotator to label these 2 objects (use
the most prominent object between the 2 options as the object of interest).
2) Instrument Readout: Most of the data I uploaded should focus on only a
single instrument, so considering the whole image as the ROI should be fine
in general. For data that includes multiple instruments, I suggest skipping
them for now.

In the meantime, I will check with my colleagues over the next few days to
see if we can re-upload datasets with these pre-filled attributes to make
them more representative.
Apologies for missing these details.

And yes, the production dataset will include these pre-filled attributes.

subject: Re: Encord/Zipline - Renewal
text:
Hi Alyssa- thanks for this. I wanted to share thoughts and perspective for
how we got here. The LiDAR contract is still off on it's own, so it's not
contemplated here.

In apples to apples, we've paid for the Encord "Platform" of $77,350
[includes 10 users, 6.25M GPU credits], + $6,650 for 8 users = ~$84k
total. That was for a 1 year deal.

We are largely off on the "Platform" cost being carried over consistent
with our previous pricing.

The additional 40 users at $500 seems reasonable to me.

The additional workspace of $25k seems reasonable to me.

The paid support package...what is this getting us above and beyond what we
have previously had to justify the $50k/year?

Finally, it's not reasonable for us to prepay in advance effectively this
whole contract. I would say we should be prorating the amount to the
October 1st 2026 timeline, and then having the annual invoice + the $55k
annual invoice from LiDAR kick in then. Consider the prorated portion being
billed now a discount reflecting the 18 months of commitment instead of the
12 months.

So in total I expect that we arrive at:
Platform: $77,350 [includes 10 users & 6.25M GPU]
Additional Users: $20,000 [40 users]
Additional Workspace: $25,000
FDE Support Package: TBD

Best,
Will

subject: Re: Encord // Tools for Humanity - platform demo
text:
Hi Hugo,

Apologies for the late reply — I was out of office last week.

At the moment, we’re coming from a largely in-house solution, but with the increasing scale of our labeling operations we’re evaluating whether an external solution can give us more efficiency and stronger model integration / pre-labeling capabilities, while maintaining the security and privacy standards we currently have.

Concretely, it would be great to cover the following areas:

• 

Data privacy & security: Full control over data in our AWS S3 buckets, ideally via self-hosted deployment with no data leaving our environment.

• 

Data visualization & exploration: Scalable dataset browsing (10M+ images) with filtering, tagging, and metadata-based queries (e.g. confidence, embeddings, timestamps), plus the ability to send data directly into labeling workflows. Nice to have: embedding visualization and similarity search.

• 

Annotation capabilities: Support for bounding boxes, segmentation, keypoints, and classification, with a responsive UI (low latency, shortcuts), batch labeling, and multi-frame support.

• 

Pre-labeling & human-in-the-loop workflows: Integration with internal and external models, configurable pipelines (including multi-vote setups), batch pre-labeling, confidence-based routing, and review/audit loops with commenting.

• 

Workforce management: Role-based access (admin/annotator/reviewer), task assignment, and performance tracking (e.g. throughput, quality metrics).

• 

Dataset management & versioning: Ability to create datasets via filtered labels, visualize subsets, maintain version control, and track dataset lineage.

• 

API & SDK support: Python SDK, robust REST APIs for dataset/pipeline/annotation management, and webhooks for automation.

Looking forward to the session!

Best,
